claim.pdf_says: 8.4.3.4.4 General rule 1 lists the applicable INVOKE forms one per line. Page 163 prints: "INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier" then "INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier"; page 164 continues with "INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier" then "INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier", followed by a separate paragraph "where:" and then items a) b) c).
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 7078 (end of the page-163 slice): "INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier where:" — three of the four printed forms plus the "where:" lead-in run together on a single line.
claim.why_it_matters: General rule 1 defines the semantics of an inline method invocation by equivalence to one of four distinct INVOKE statement forms. Merged onto one line they read as a single unparsable statement, so the boundaries between the four alternatives (and hence which forms exist) are no longer recoverable, and the "where:" lead-in that governs items a)-c) on page 164 is buried inside that line, orphaning those definitions.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED as a content discrepancy. Both of the claim's factual observations are ACCURATE, but the difference is newline placement inside a display block that spans a page break — the explicitly excluded 'page-break furniture / line wrapping / formatting' class — and it changes no meaning.

WHAT THE PDF ACTUALLY PRINTS (rendered at 300 dpi, E:/Temp/specrecon/v163/spec_p163.png = printed folio 133, and E:/Temp/specrecon/v164/spec_p164.png = printed folio 134). Page 163 ends 8.4.3.4.4 GR 1 with a two-line sans-serif display block: 'INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier' / 'INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier', and then nothing but the '(c)ISO/IEC 2023  133' footer — there is no clipped third line. Page 164 opens with the two remaining display lines 'INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier' / 'INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier', then a standalone serif paragraph 'where:', then hanging-indent items a), b), c). So the claim's description of both pages is correct, and the two object-class-name-1 forms plus 'where:' do belong to page 164.

WHAT THE MARKDOWN ACTUALLY HAS (exact bytes, specs/ISO_COBOL.md): 7075 = the GR-1 lead paragraph ending 'as follows:'; 7076 blank; 7077 = '   INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier'; 7078 = '   INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier where:'; 7079 blank; 7080-7082 the page-164 anchor/heading/running head; 7085 = 'a) arguments are the operands ...'. The claim quotes line 7078 verbatim. So both sides are quoted correctly and this is a genuine raw-source line-break defect, not a slicing artifact.

WHY IT IS REJECTED ANYWAY.
(1) NOTHING IS MISSING, ADDED, OR REORDERED. I compared the joined line word-for-word against the rendered glyphs of the three PDF display lines and the 'where:' paragraph: all four INVOKE forms are present verbatim (both 'identifier-1' forms, both 'object-class-name-1' forms, each with its USING/RETURNING phrasing intact), 'where:' is present with its colon, and a), b), c) follow in correct sequence. Reading the file sequentially yields exactly the PDF's reading order.
(2) THE FORM BOUNDARIES ARE TRIVIALLY RECOVERABLE, so the claim's central harm is false. Each alternative begins with the keyword 'INVOKE' and ends with 'temp-identifier'; the word INVOKE occurs exactly four times in the merged text. A reader or a consumer cannot mistake this for 'a single unparsable statement' any more than the p255 precedent's joined 'a) ... b) ... c) ...' could be mistaken for one item — there the a)/b)/c) glyphs carried the boundaries, here the INVOKE keyword does. 'Which forms exist' is not lost.
(3) THE 'where:' LEAD-IN IS NOT ORPHANED. It sits immediately before items a)-c) in reading order, separated only by the page-anchor furniture that separates every construct straddling a page break in this transcription. Nothing else intervenes, and a)-c) define exactly the two terms ('arguments', 'temp-identifier') used in the forms above, so the governance relation is unambiguous.
(4) THE MERGE IS RENDERING-INVISIBLE UNDER THIS FILE'S OWN CONVENTION. Lines 7077-7078 are three-space-indented lazy continuation lines of one paragraph — not a fenced code block. In CommonMark they already join with a single space regardless of the newline between them, so a 'corrected' 4-separate-lines transcription would render identically. The only rendering-relevant residue is that 'where:' is not its own paragraph, which is cosmetic given (3).
(5) NO CHOICE INDICATOR OR ENUMERATOR IS INVOLVED. Looking at the printed glyphs myself: the display block carries no markers at all — no bullets, no a)/b)/c), no braces or brackets — just four bare sans-serif statement lines. There is therefore no choice indicator to lose. (The one figure on page 163 that does use choice delimiters, the 8.4.3.4.2 general format, is transcribed separately at lines 7057-7063 with its braces/brackets and the 'OMITTED' underline noted, and is not part of this claim.)

Distinguishing precedent: this is the p255 pattern (peer items joined across a page break with their own leading markers intact → real=false), not the p155 pattern (a structural 'Format 3 (reference-modification):' LABEL absorbed into a different format's body paragraph, which destroyed a delimiter and created a false reading → real=true). 'where:' is boilerplate prose adjacent to what it governs, not a section label whose loss removes a boundary.

Residual, sub-threshold: whoever next touches this region could split line 7078 into three lines and give 'where:' its own paragraph, and ideally fence all four forms as a display block. That is a cosmetic fidelity polish, not a spec-content discrepancy, and it affects no derivation of INVOKE or inline-method-invocation semantics.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The transcription does merge PDF page 164's two object-class-name-1 INVOKE forms and its standalone 'where:' paragraph onto the tail of specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 7078, ahead of the page-164 anchor — a raw-source line-break/paragraph-boundary defect. But all four INVOKE forms, 'where:', and items a)-c) are present verbatim and in correct reading order; each form is still delimited by its own leading 'INVOKE' keyword so no alternative is lost or ambiguous; 'where:' remains immediately adjacent to the a)-c) items it governs; and because lines 7077-7078 are lazy paragraph continuations rather than a fenced block, the internal newline carries no rendered meaning under this file's own convention. The claim's asserted harms — 'boundaries no longer recoverable' and definitions 'orphaned' — are both overstated. At most a cosmetic polish (split line 7078 into three lines, give 'where:' its own paragraph, optionally fence the block); no impact on derived semantics.
